# PearBrowser

> PearBrowser is a free, open-source desktop browser for the regular and peer-to-peer web. It opens hyper:// sites, discovers verified apps, publishes directly to peers, and keeps identity and browsing data local-first without tracking its users.

## Privacy promise

- PearBrowser ships with no usage telemetry, remote analytics, advertising network, or tracking SDK.
- PearBrowser does not upload browsing history to an analytics, advertising, or profiling service.
- Browsing history and local full-text page indexing are disabled by default.
- If the user enables history or local search indexing, that data is stored locally unless the user explicitly enables encrypted device sync.
- Content Shield, HTTPS-only navigation, tracking-parameter stripping, third-party cookie blocking, and fingerprint farbling are enabled by default.
- PearBrowser does not require a central account.
- PearBrowser Home opens as the active first tab with DuckDuckGo web search. PearBrowser sends no search analytics and excludes submitted searches from its optional persistent visit log.
- DuckDuckGo receives the query and network address to return results. Its published policy says it does not save or share search history. This is private search, not anonymity.
- PearBrowser is private, not anonymous. Websites, relay operators, and P2P peers may receive network metadata needed to serve content.
- Some HiveRelay operators support optional Tor endpoints, but PearBrowser Desktop does not yet route browser traffic through Tor automatically.

## Product facts

- Current desktop release: v0.8.0.
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- Current desktop packages are SHA-256-verifiable package-proof builds, not public-trust installers. macOS is ad-hoc signed but not notarized; Windows is unsigned.
- Signed catalogue v11 carries 14 apps. Native Pear v3 submissions bind canonical production identity, product, version and targets to one signed receipt and may include a bounded byte-validated icon.
- PearBrowser can browse ordinary HTTPS websites and native hyper:// peer-to-peer sites.
- Its desktop interface provides familiar tabs, addresses, search, app discovery, publishing, identity, and permission prompts over a local Bare backend that handles Hyperdrive storage, verification, and Hyperswarm peer connections.
- The browser includes a private-search home powered by DuckDuckGo, decentralized app catalogues, local-first Lighthouse search, P2P publishing, browser-owned Content Shield lists, and capability-gated Pear Plugins.
- Source license: Apache-2.0.
